# hashCode

<link-summary>Produces a numeric hash for any value.</link-summary>

<web-summary>hashCode() — Produces a numeric hash for any value. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/object</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function hashCode(value: unknown): number;
```

The value is turned into a string first — an object through the key-sorted form `stringifyJson` produces — and the string is folded into a 32-bit integer. Two values that `equals` considers equal hash the same.

It is a bucket key, not a checksum: different values can collide, and the result is not stable across releases of the library.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description        |
| :-------- | :-------- | :----------------- |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to hash. |

## Returns

`number` — a 32-bit integer; `0` for an empty string.

## Examples

### Hashing

```javascript
hashCode("abc"); // => 96354
hashCode(""); // => 0
```
